mainTopic: The צריכותא of the three פסח פסוקים, מבוג's teaching on נחשון's חטאת, changing between kinds of חטאת or owners, and intent from one עבודה to another
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. Three פסוקים teach that a leftover קרבן פסח is brought as a שלמים, and the גמרא shows that each one is needed for a different situation of the animal. Next, רב quotes מבוג about a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of נחשון's חטאת. רב משרשיא challenges the first version from a ברייתא about מנחות. The גמרא then reworks מבוג's teaching several times, ending with two versions that both treat נחשון's חטאת as an עולה. רב rules on a חטאת for חלב slaughtered in the name of other kinds of חטאת, and רבא asks about the חטאת for טומאת מקדש. רב אחא בריה דרבא teaches that every such change makes the offering פסולה, and moves רבא's teachings over to a change of owner. רבא's question ends in תיקו. Finally, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about a חטאת slaughtered לשמה with a plan to sprinkle its blood שלא לשמה, and the גמרא begins to show that each follows his usual reasoning, a point that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Three verses for three different situations
steps.stepSummary: Each of the three פסוקים is assigned to a different case of a פסח animal: time and year both passed, time passed but not the year, or neither passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: One פסוק is for a case where the animal's time passed and its year passed. One is for where its time passed but not its year. And one is for where neither its time nor its year passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why there are three פסוקים: each one teaches the rule for a different kind of פסח animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Its time" means the time for bringing the פסח, and "its year" means the animal's first year, after which it can no longer be a פסח. The three cases range from completely ruled out as a פסח to still fully fit. Each פסוק teaches that in its case the animal can be brought as a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Passed, went by
Its time, the time for bringing the פסח
Its year, the animal's first year of life
One (here: one פסוק)

phrases.english: One verse is for where its time passed and its year passed,
and one is for where its time passed but not its year,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד לְלֹא עִיבְּרָה לֹא זְמַנּוֹ וְלֹא שְׁנָתוֹ.
phrases.english: and one is for where neither its time nor its year passed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the three פסוקים by giving each one its own case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the תורה need three separate פסוקים for this rule?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each פסוק covers a different situation: time and year passed, time passed only, or neither passed.

steps.title: Why one verse would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: With only one פסוק, we would apply the rule only to an animal fully ruled out as a פסח, and not to one still fit for פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them are needed. If the תורה had written only one, I would have said: that is where its year and its time both passed, because it is completely ruled out from being a פסח. But where its time passed and not its year, since it is still fit for פסח שני, I would say no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins proving that all three פסוקים are needed. First it shows why a single פסוק would not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal whose time and year have both passed can never be a פסח again, so it makes sense that it becomes a שלמים. An animal whose year has not passed can still serve on פסח שני, so we might think it keeps its פסח status. That is why a second פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed (each one teaches something)
The Merciful One, the תורה
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
Was pushed away, ruled out
The second פסח, a month after the first

steps.confusionAlert: Here "one" means the case where both time and year passed. The גמרא is not yet talking about the third case, where neither passed; that comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And they are needed; for if the Merciful One had written only one,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: הֵיכָא דְּעִיבְּרָה שְׁנָתוֹ וּזְמַנּוֹ –
phrases.english: I would have said: where its year and its time have passed,
since it is completely ruled out from being a פסח;
but where its time passed and not its year,
since it is still fit for the second פסח,
I would say no.
phrases.notes: He means: I would say it is not brought as a שלמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Justifies the split of the three cases in step 1 by showing that the first case cannot teach the second.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source teaches a case the other cannot
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With one פסוק, only an animal fully ruled out as a פסח would become a שלמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: A second פסוק is needed for an animal still fit for פסח שני.

steps.title: Why two verses would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: Even with two פסוקים, we would not apply the rule to an animal that is still fit for the פסח itself, so the third פסוק is needed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written only these two, I would say it is because they were both ruled out from their purpose. But where neither its time nor its year passed, since it is still fit for the פסח, I would say no. So all three are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא, showing that two פסוקים would still leave out the third case, and concludes that all three are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two cases have something in common: in each, the animal has been ruled out from its original purpose. In the third case nothing has happened yet, and the animal is still fully fit for the פסח, so we might think it cannot become a שלמים. The third פסוק teaches that it can.

keyTerms.meaning: Two
From their purpose, from what they were meant for
I would say no

steps.whatToRemember: Three פסוקים, three cases: fully ruled out, ruled out only from the first פסח, and still fully fit. Each case is stronger than the one before, so each needs its own פסוק to teach that the animal can be a שלמים.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written these two,
I would say it is because they were ruled out from their purpose;
but where there has not passed
either its time or its year,
since it is fit for the פסח,
I would say no. So they are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא from step 2 by explaining the need for the third פסוק, and closes with צריכי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three פסוקים are needed, since each case could not be learned from the others.

steps.title: A sin offering slaughtered for the sake of נחשון's sin offering
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoting מבוג, rules that a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of a חטאת like נחשון's is כשרה, because the פסוק teaches one law for all חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said in the name of מבוג: A חטאת that someone slaughtered for the sake of the חטאת of נחשון is כשרה, because the פסוק says "This is the law of the חטאת", meaning one law for all the חטאות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב reports a ruling from מבוג about a חטאת slaughtered with the wrong kind of חטאת in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחשון's חטאת was a gift brought at the dedication of the משכן, not to atone for a sin. You might think that slaughtering a regular חטאת with that different kind in mind would disqualify it. מבוג learns from the פסוק that all חטאות share one law, so this does not count as changing it into something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering
נחשון בן עמינדב, the first נשיא to bring a קרבן at the dedication of the משכן
Valid, acceptable
For the sake of, with the intent of
One law

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a new discussion: does thinking of a different kind of חטאת count as a wrong intent? מבוג's answer is that all חטאות form one category.

phrases.english: Rav said in the name of Mavog:

phrases.aramaic: חַטָּאת שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ לְשׁוּם חַטַּאת נַחְשׁוֹן – כְּשֵׁירָה;
phrases.english: A sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of the sin offering of Nahshon is valid;
phrases.notes: נחשון's חטאת was brought at the dedication of the משכן as a gift, not for a sin (במדבר 7).

phrases.english: for the verse says: "This is the law of the sin offering",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:18

phrases.english: one law for all the sin offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement, unconnected to the צריכותא about the פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת slaughtered for the sake of a חטאת like נחשון's is כשרה, since all חטאות share one law.

steps.title: רב משרשיא brings a ברייתא of רבי שמעון about מנחות
steps.stepSummary: רבא repeats מבוג's teaching. רב משרשיא answers with a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says מנחות whose handful was taken for the wrong kind of מנחה are כשרות and still count for the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא sat and said this teaching. רב משרשיא objected to רבא from a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says, all meal offerings whose handful was removed not for their own sake are valid, and they count for the owners as their required offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא repeats מבוג's teaching, and רב משרשיא starts an objection by quoting a ברייתא. This step only sets up the objection; the actual challenge comes in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא brings in a new subject, מנחות. רבי שמעון holds that a מנחה whose handful was taken for the wrong type of מנחה is כשרה and even counts for the owner's obligation. The next lines of the ברייתא give the reason, and the challenge is built on that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Flour offerings (meal offerings)
The handful (קֹמֶץ) was removed, the key service of a מִנְחָה
Not for their own sake, meaning for the sake of a different offering
It counts for the owners as fulfilling their obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב משרשיא is arguing about מנחות for their own sake. He brings this ברייתא only to test מבוג's 'one law for all' reasoning.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רָבָא וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא;
phrases.english: Rava sat and was saying this teaching;
phrases.notes: 'This teaching' is מבוג's rule from step 4 about a חטאת slaughtered for the sake of נחשון's חטאת.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya raised an objection to Rava:
Rabbi Shimon says:
All meal offerings from which a handful was removed not for their own sake
are valid, and they count for the owners as their obligation;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an objection against מבוג's rule from step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: מבוג's teaching that one פסוק makes one law for all חטאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The setup only: it brings a ברייתא about מנחות whose reasoning will be used against מבוג in step 8.

steps.title: The reason: a meal offering's preparation shows what it is
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that מנחות are different from animal offerings. A מנחה's preparation shows its true type, so a wrong intention cannot change it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because meal offerings are not like animal offerings. If someone removes the handful from a pan-fried מנחה for the sake of a deep-pan מנחה, its preparation shows that it is a pan-fried one. If he removes it from a dry מנחה for the sake of one mixed with oil, its preparation shows that it is a dry one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives רבי שמעון's reason. Each type of מנחה is made in its own way, so anyone can see what kind it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wrong thought is plainly false when the offering's own preparation contradicts it. Because the intention is obviously wrong, it does not take effect, and the מנחה still counts. This reason, 'its preparation proves', is the key point רב משרשיא will build on.

keyTerms.meaning: A מִנְחָה made in a flat, shallow pan
A מִנְחָה made in a deep pan
Its preparation proves (shows) what it really is
A dry מִנְחָה with no oil mixed in
A מִנְחָה mixed with oil

phrases.english: Because meal offerings are not similar to animal offerings.
For one who removes the handful from a shallow-pan offering for the sake of a deep-pan offering:
its preparation proves about it that it is a shallow-pan offering;
a dry offering for the sake of one mixed with oil:
its preparation proves that it is a dry offering;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא by giving the reason for רבי שמעון's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מנחה counts despite a wrong intention because its preparation openly proves its true type.

steps.title: Animal offerings all look the same
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא contrasts זבחים: their slaughter, receiving of the blood, and sprinkling are done the same way for every type, so nothing proves which offering it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with animal offerings it is not so. There is one slaughter for all of them, one receiving of the blood for all of them, and one sprinkling for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by explaining why זבחים are different. With animal offerings, the actions look identical no matter which offering it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nothing visible proves the offering's type, a wrong intention can take effect on a זבח. That is why a זבח done for the wrong sake does not count for the owner, unlike a מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal offerings
Slaughtering the animal
Receiving the blood in a vessel
Sprinkling or throwing the blood on the מִזְבֵּחַ

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's rule: a מנחה counts despite a wrong intention only because its preparation proves what it is. זבחים have no such proof.

phrases.english: But with animal offerings it is not so:
there is one slaughter for all of them,
one receiving of the blood for all of them,
one sprinkling for all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by contrasting זבחים with מנחות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With זבחים, every service looks the same for all types, so a wrong intention takes effect.

steps.title: Why not one law for all meal offerings?
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא infers from the ברייתא that when preparation does not prove the type, the מנחה would not count. But by מבוג's reasoning, 'זאת תורת המנחה' should make one law for all מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that its preparation proves what it is. So if its preparation does not prove it, it would not count. Why not? Let us say: 'This is the law of the meal offering', meaning one law for all meal offerings!
steps.whatsHappening: Now רב משרשיא makes his actual challenge. He reads a hidden rule out of the ברייתא's reason and shows that it clashes with מבוג's way of reading פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets a מנחה count only when its preparation proves its type. That implies that without such proof it would not count. But if מבוג is right that 'תורת החטאת' means one law for all חטאות, then 'תורת המנחה' should also mean one law for all מנחות, so every מנחה should count, even without proof from its preparation.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is… (used to draw an inference from the reason given)
But then, meaning the opposite case
Why?
One law, the same rule for every type

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge tests whether מבוג's reading of 'תורת' as 'one law for all' can really be correct, since the same reading would contradict רבי שמעון's ברייתא.

phrases.english: The reason is that its preparation proves what it is;
but if its preparation does not prove it, it would not count;
Why? Let us say:
'This is the law of the meal offering':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:7

phrases.english: one law for all meal offerings!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּמַעֲשֶׂיהָ מוֹכִיחִין, הָא אֵין מַעֲשֶׂיהָ מוֹכִיחִין לָא; אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא's reason and turns it into a challenge against מבוג
steps.kashyaTarget: מבוג's teaching that 'תורת' means one law for all types
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies a מנחה whose preparation does not prove its type would not count. Yet by מבוג's method, 'זאת תורת המנחה' should make all מנחות count no matter what.

steps.title: A new version of מבוג's ruling: no atonement for the dead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a different version of מבוג's teaching. The חטאת is כשרה because a dead person like נחשון cannot receive כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, it was said like this: רב said in the name of מבוג: A חטאת slaughtered so that נחשון would get atonement through it is fit, because there is no atonement for the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the challenge from מנחות, the גמרא gives up the earlier version of מבוג's teaching. It replaces it with a new version that rests on a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old reason was 'one law for all חטאות', and the מנחות challenge knocked it down. The new reason is that a dead person cannot get כפרה at all. So naming נחשון is not a real change of owner (שינוי בעלים), and the offering stays כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, it was said like this. This opens a corrected version of a teaching.
On condition that he be atoned for by it
There is no atonement for the dead
The נשיא of שבט יהודה, who had died long before

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same statement as before. Step 4 said the חטאת is כשרה because of 'one law for all חטאות'. Here the reason is completely different: a dead person cannot get atonement.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated,
phrases.notes: 'It' means מבוג's teaching. The earlier version could not stand after the מנחות challenge.

phrases.english: it was stated like this:
Rav said in the name of Mavog:
A sin offering that one slaughtered
on condition that Nahshon be atoned for by it
is fit;
there is no atonement for the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by replacing the original version of מבוג's statement with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restating the teaching with a different reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מבוג ruled the חטאת is כשרה because all חטאות share one law.
steps.terutzMaskana: מבוג ruled it is כשרה because a dead person cannot receive כפרה, so naming him is not a real change of owner.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת slaughtered for נחשון's atonement is כשרה, since there is no כפרה for the dead.

steps.title: Why mention נחשון and not just any dead person
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is that the dead have no כפרה, why did מבוג pick נחשון in particular?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him just say 'a dead person' in general!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new version. If death is the whole reason, naming נחשון seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any dead person would fit the rule 'no atonement for the dead'. Choosing נחשון in particular suggests he had some extra point in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say
In general, just any

phrases.english: But let him say just any dead person!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the new version given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The specific mention of נחשון in מבוג's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If death alone makes the חטאת כשרה, any dead person would do, so naming נחשון looks unnecessary.

steps.title: A living person like נחשון would make it פסולה
steps.stepSummary: Naming נחשון teaches that only death makes it כשרה. For a living person in a similar situation, such as a נזיר or a מצורע, the חטאת would be פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he teaches us: the reason it is fit is that he is dead. But for a living person similar to נחשון, it is unfit. And who is that? Someone bringing the חטאת of a נזיר or the חטאת of a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that מבוג named נחשון on purpose. It teaches a hidden rule about living people who are similar to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחשון's חטאת was not brought for a sin, and neither are the חטאת of a נזיר or of a מצורע. Since a living person can still get כפרה, slaughtering a regular חטאת for him counts as a change of owner and makes it פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he teaches us
Similar to
The חטאת a נזיר brings when he finishes his נזירות
The חטאת a מצורע brings when he becomes pure

phrases.english: This is what he teaches us:
the reason it is fit is that he is dead;
but for a living person
similar to Nahshon, it is unfit.
phrases.notes: Similar how? Like נחשון's, this person's חטאת is not brought because of a sin.

phrases.english: And what is that?
The sin offering of a nazirite and the sin offering of a leper.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: טַעְמָא דְּמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by explaining why נחשון was named.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise wording teaches a hidden rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning נחשון adds nothing beyond 'any dead person'.
steps.terutzMaskana: Naming נחשון implies that a living person in a similar situation (a נזיר or מצורע) makes the חטאת פסולה.

steps.title: But a נזיר's and a מצורע's חטאת are like עולות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the חטאת of a נזיר or a מצורע is not for a sin, so it is like an עולה. Why would slaughtering for such a person make the חטאת פסולה?
steps.simpleTranslation: These are like עולות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It argues that the חטאת of a נזיר or a מצורע should not cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since these offerings do not come to atone for a sin, they act like עולות. Slaughtering a חטאת for someone who owes an עולה is not a real change of owner. So the חטאת should not become פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offerings, which are not brought to atone for a specific sin
They are

phrases.english: These are burnt offerings!
phrases.notes: He means they work like עולות, since they are not brought to atone for a sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 11 that a חטאת slaughtered for a נזיר or מצורע is פסולה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a living person like נחשון (a נזיר or מצורע) makes the חטאת פסולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their חטאות are not for a sin, so they are like עולות. Slaughtering a חטאת for someone who owes an עולה is not a change of owner, so it should not become פסולה.

steps.title: מבוג's teaching restated: a sin offering for someone like נחשון is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a corrected version of מבוג's teaching. A חטאת slaughtered for a person who owes a חטאת like נחשון's is כשרה, because נחשון's חטאת is really like an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this teaching was said, this is how it was said. רב said in the name of מבוג: a חטאת that someone slaughtered for a person who owes a חטאת like נחשון's is כשרה, because נחשון's חטאת counts as an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier version, which said a living נזיר or מצורע would make the חטאת פסולה. It replaces it with a version that says the חטאת is כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 pointed out that the חטאת of a נזיר or a מצורע does not come for a sin, so it is like an עולה. The new version agrees with this. Slaughtering for a person whose חטאת works like an עולה is like slaughtering for someone who owes an עולה, so the חטאת stays כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said. This is a formula for restating a teaching in corrected form.
The נשיא of שבט יהודה, who brought a חטאת at the dedication of the מזבח.
Obligated; someone who owes an offering.
Valid; the offering is accepted.
Burnt offering. It is not brought to atone for a specific sin.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is setting aside the version from Steps 9–11 and giving the teaching in a new form.

phrases.english: Rav said in the name of Mavog:
A sin offering that one slaughtered
for one who is obligated to bring a sin offering like Nahshon's
is valid;
Nahshon's sin offering is like a burnt offering.
phrases.notes: נחשון's חטאת was not brought for any sin, so the גמרא treats it like an עולה. See במדבר 7:16.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by replacing the version of מבוג's teaching that Step 12 attacked.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewriting the version of the teaching that was challenged.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Slaughtering for a living person whose חטאת does not come for a sin, such as a נזיר or a מצורע, makes the חטאת פסולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Such a חטאת is like an עולה, so slaughtering for that person leaves the חטאת כשרה.

steps.title: A second version: a sin offering slaughtered in the name of נחשון's offering is invalid
steps.stepSummary: Another version of מבוג's teaching says that a חטאת slaughtered in the name of נחשון's חטאת is פסולה, because נחשון's חטאת is like an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רב said in the name of מבוג: a חטאת that someone slaughtered in the name of נחשון's חטאת is פסולה, because נחשון's חטאת counts as an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different report of מבוג's teaching. In this report, the case is about the kind of offering, not about the person it is slaughtered for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that נחשון's חטאת is like an עולה. Here that fact leads to the opposite result. Slaughtering a חטאת 'in the name of' an offering that is really an עולה is like slaughtering it as an עולה, which is a change of offering type, so it is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: There is one who says; this introduces another version of the same teaching.
In the name of; with the intention of a particular offering.
Invalid; the offering is not accepted.

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the small word change. Step 13 says על, slaughtered for a person, and the חטאת is כשרה. Here it says לְשֵׁם, slaughtered in the name of a type of offering, and the חטאת is פסולה. Both rulings rest on the same idea that נחשון's חטאת is like an עולה.

phrases.english: There is one who says:
Rav said in the name of Mavog:
A sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of Nahshon's sin offering
is invalid;
Nahshon's sin offering is like a burnt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second report of the same teaching as Step 13. It uses the same reason to reach the opposite result in a different case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת slaughtered in the name of נחשון's חטאת is פסולה, because that is like slaughtering it as an עולה.

steps.title: Why not mention a nazirite's or a leper's sin offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why מבוג used נחשון's חטאת, which no one brings anymore, instead of the חטאת of a נזיר or a מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say 'the חטאת of a נזיר' and 'the חטאת of a מצורע'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the example מבוג chose. The חטאת of a נזיר or a מצורע is also like an עולה, and people actually bring those offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends only on the fact that the חטאת is like an עולה. The חטאת of a נזיר and of a מצורע share that feature. So why pick a one-time offering from the dedication of the מזבח?

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say; this introduces a challenge asking for a better example.
A person who took a vow of נזירות.
A person with צרעת.

phrases.english: But let him say:
A nazirite's sin offering and a leper's sin offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the example used in both versions of מבוג's teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: מבוג's choice of נחשון as the example.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חטאת of a נזיר and of a מצורע are also like an עולה, and they are common, so they would make a more natural example.

steps.title: He chose the original sin offering
steps.stepSummary: מבוג named נחשון because his was the first and main example of a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took the main חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that מבוג chose the first and most basic example of a חטאת that is like an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law itself is the same for a נזיר and a מצורע. מבוג simply picked the original case: נחשון's חטאת was the first individual חטאת mentioned in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The main or original one.
He took; he chose this as his example.

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions of מבוג's teaching, נחשון's חטאת is like an עולה. Slaughtering a חטאת for a person who owes such a חטאת leaves it כשרה. Slaughtering a חטאת in the name of such a חטאת makes it פסולה. נחשון is named only because his was the first such חטאת.

phrases.english: He cited the primary sin offering.
phrases.notes: נחשון's was the first individual חטאת brought, so it is the classic example.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming נחשון must point to some special law that applies only to his case.
steps.terutzMaskana: נחשון was chosen only because his was the first and main example of such a חטאת.

steps.title: One kind of sin offering slaughtered in the name of another kind stays valid
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a חטאת brought for eating חלב, if slaughtered in the name of a חטאת for eating דם or for עבודה זרה, is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: a חטאת for eating חלב that someone slaughtered in the name of a חטאת for eating דם, or in the name of a חטאת for עבודה זרה, is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new teaching from רב. Switching between different kinds of חטאת does not count as changing the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת becomes פסולה when it is slaughtered as a different type of offering. Here every case is still a חטאת; only the sin it comes for is different. So רב treats it as the same offering, and it stays כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fats of an animal; eating them by mistake requires a חטאת.
Blood; eating it by mistake also requires a חטאת.
Idol worship.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the 'name' of a חטאת is its type as a חטאת, not the specific sin it atones for. That idea will matter as the sugya goes on.

phrases.english: Rav said:
A sin offering for forbidden fat that one slaughtered
for the sake of a sin offering for blood,
or for the sake of a sin offering for idol worship
is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חַטַּאת חֵלֶב שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ לְשֵׁם חַטַּאת דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching from רב about changing between kinds of חטאת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering one kind of חטאת in the name of another kind of חטאת does not make it פסולה.

steps.title: Slaughtered in the name of a נזיר's or מצורע's sin offering, it is unfit
steps.stepSummary: רב finishes his ruling. A חטאת for חלב slaughtered in the name of a נזיר's or מצורע's חטאת is פסולה, because those offerings are like an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he slaughtered it in the name of a נזיר's חטאת or a מצורע's חטאת, it is unfit, because those are really like burnt offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב's ruling from the last step. This half covers the cases where the offering becomes unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the name from חלב to דם or עבודה זרה kept the offering כשרה, because all of these are true חטאות that atone for a sin. A נזיר's or מצורע's חטאת does not atone for any sin, so it counts as a completely different type of offering, like an עולה. That makes the offering פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow to avoid wine and haircuts; he brings a חטאת when his vow ends
A person with צרעת; he brings a חטאת as part of his purification
Unfit, the offering does not count
Burnt offerings, which do not come to atone for a specific sin

steps.whatToRemember: According to this version of רב: changing to another חטאת that atones for a sin is כשרה, but changing to a נזיר's or מצורע's חטאת is פסולה, because those are like an עולה.

phrases.english: For the sake of a nazir's sin offering,
for the sake of a metzora's sin offering, it is unfit;
these are burnt offerings.
phrases.notes: They don't come to wipe away a sin, so they count like an עולה. This is the same idea used for נחשון's חטאת earlier.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְשֵׁם חַטַּאת נָזִיר, לְשֵׁם חַטַּאת מְצוֹרָע – פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב's ruling from step 17 by giving the cases where the offering becomes unfit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת for חלב slaughtered in the name of a נזיר's or מצורע's חטאת is פסולה, since those are like an עולה.

steps.title: רבא asks about slaughtering in the name of the sin offering for impurity of the Temple
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about a חטאת for חלב slaughtered in the name of the חטאת for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. Is it כשרה because both sins carry כרת? Or is it פסולה because that offering is not fixed like the חטאת for חלב?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: a חטאת for חלב that was slaughtered in the name of the חטאת for making the מקדש or its holy foods impure, what is the law? Do we say it is like the חלב offering, because both sins carry כרת? Or perhaps it is different, because that offering is not fixed the way the חלב offering is?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new question about a borderline case that falls between the two halves of רב's ruling. He gives the reasons for both sides. The question comes back in a new form in step 23 and ends in תיקו in step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On one side, the sin of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו carries כרת, just like eating חלב, so the offering looks like a fellow 'real' חטאת. On the other side, its offering is a קרבן עולה ויורד, which changes with how much money the person has, while the חלב offering is always an animal. So the question is which feature makes two חטאות count as 'the same kind': sharing כרת, or both being a fixed offering.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, raised a question
Entering the מקדש or eating holy food while impure
A heavenly punishment of being cut off, given for doing certain sins on purpose
Fixed: an offering that is always the same animal, no matter how rich or poor the person is
Or perhaps, introducing the other side of the question

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse קבוע here with the 'עולה' comparison from before. Both offerings here atone for a sin. The question is only about the fixed offering versus the one that changes with a person's wealth.

phrases.english: Rava asks:
A sin offering for forbidden fat that he slaughtered
for the sake of a sin offering for impurity of the Temple and its sacred foods,
what is the law?
Do we say: it carries karet just like it;
phrases.notes: So it is a 'real' חטאת like the חלב one, and should be כשרה.

phrases.english: or perhaps,
it is not fixed like it?
phrases.notes: The טומאת מקדש offering changes with how much money the person has. The חלב offering is always an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רב's rule about which name changes keep the offering כשרה and tests it on a case that sits in between.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a חטאת for חלב slaughtered in the name of the חטאת for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו כשרה, because both carry כרת, or פסולה, because one is fixed and the other is not?

steps.title: רב אחא son of רבא teaches that every case is unfit
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא teaches רב's ruling differently: in every case, even in the name of the חטאת for דם or עבודה זרה, the offering is פסולה. His source is 'ושחט אותה לחטאת', meaning it must be slaughtered for that very חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, the son of רבא, teaches that all of these cases are unfit. Why? Because the פסוק says 'and he shall slaughter it for a sin offering', which means for the sake of that exact sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of רב's ruling. In this version, every name change makes the חטאת unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version allowed a change to another sin-atoning חטאת. This version says any change at all ruins the offering. The proof is the word 'אותה' ('it'), which teaches that the חטאת must be slaughtered in the name of the exact same sin it was brought for, not just any חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches, meaning he passes down the ruling in this version
All of them, meaning every case
As unfit
It, meaning that very one

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רב. In the first, changing to another real חטאת is כשרה. In רב אחא בריה דרבא's version, any change is פסולה, because of 'ושחט אותה לחטאת'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the very idea of 'same kind of חטאת' is debated. The answer decides whether a small name change between two חטאות makes the offering unfit.

phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava,
teaches all of them as unfit,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' includes the דם and עבודה זרה cases that רב called כשרה in the first version.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
"And he shall slaughter it for a sin offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:33

phrases.english: for the sake of that very sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מַתְנֵי כּוּלְּהוּ לִפְסוּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of רב's ruling (steps 17-18), in which every name change is פסולה. This also makes רבא's question unnecessary.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת slaughtered in the name of any other חטאת is פסולה, because 'ושחט אותה לחטאת' requires the name of that exact חטאת.

steps.title: רב אשי asks how רבא's question fits
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks רב אחא בריה דרבא how he teaches רבא's question, since his version of רב seems to leave no room for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב אחא son of רבא: How do you teach רבא's question?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks how רב אחא learns רבא's question. The question is really a hidden challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא asked whether a חטאת for חלב slaughtered in the name of the חטאת for טומאת מקדש is כשרה. That only makes sense if some changes of חטאת type leave the offering כשרה. In רב אחא's version of רב, every change makes it פסולה, so רבא's question seems to have no place.

keyTerms.meaning: A question that is asked but not yet answered
How do you (plural) teach it?

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him
to Rav Acha son of Rava:
Rava's question, how do you teach it?
phrases.notes: This is the question about טומאת מקדש from Step 19.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how Step 20's version of רב can live alongside רבא's question in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בריה דרבא's version of רב's ruling (Step 20)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If any change of חטאת type makes the offering פסולה, רבא could not have asked whether one kind of change leaves it כשרה.

steps.title: רבא's words are about a different owner
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא says his school teaches רבא's words as being about שינוי בעלים. A חטאת for חלב slaughtered for someone who owes a חטאת for דם or עבודה זרה is פסולה. If he owes a נזיר's or מצורע's חטאת, it is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We teach it as a change of owner, and this is how we teach it. רבא said: A חטאת for חלב that was slaughtered for someone who owes a חטאת for דם or a חטאת for עבודה זרה is פסולה. If it was slaughtered for someone who owes a נזיר's חטאת or a מצורע's חטאת, it is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא answers that רבא was never talking about a different kind of חטאת. He was talking about slaughtering it for a different person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is no clash with Step 20, because רבא's case is about the owner, not the type of offering. Slaughtering for another person counts as a change of owner only if that person owes a similar חטאת that brings atonement, like one for דם or עבודה זרה. A נזיר's or מצורע's חטאת is a different kind, so that person does not count, and the offering stays כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering the offering for someone other than its real owner
Owes, is required to bring
Not valid (as an offering)
Valid (as an offering)

steps.confusionAlert: The cases look the same as רב's in Steps 17-18, but the results are flipped. Here דם and עבודה זרה make it פסולה, and נזיר and מצורע leave it כשרה. That is because the topic here is the owner, not the type of offering.

phrases.english: He said to him:
We teach it as a change of owner
[and this is how we teach it]:
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets aren't in every version; they're added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A sin offering for forbidden fat that one slaughtered
for someone who owes a sin offering for blood
or a sin offering for idol worship is invalid.
For someone who owes a nazir's sin offering
or a metzora's sin offering, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the case: רבא's teaching is about a change of owner, not a change of חטאת type.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא was talking about slaughtering in the name of a different kind of חטאת, which would clash with Step 20.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא was talking about slaughtering for a different owner. That person counts only if he owes a similar חטאת that brings atonement.

steps.title: רבא's question asked again as a change of owner
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא gives רבא's question in its new form. What if the חטאת for חלב was slaughtered for someone who owes a חטאת for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו? Does it count as a change of owner because both sins carry כרת? Or not, because that offering is not fixed?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we ask the question this way. רבא asked: A חטאת for חלב that was slaughtered for someone who owes a חטאת for making the מקדש or its holy food impure: what is the law? Do we say that his sin carries כרת just like this one? Or maybe his offering is not fixed like this one?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא is still speaking. He shows how רבא's question from Step 19 reads when it is about the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides are the same as in Step 19. Now they decide whether the other person counts as a real "other owner." If his sin carries כרת like חלב, he is similar enough and the offering is פסולה. But his offering is not fixed (it changes with how much money he has), so maybe he is not similar enough and it stays כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: And we ask it this way
Like it, the same as it
Maybe, or perhaps

phrases.english: And we ask it this way:
Rava asked:
A sin offering for forbidden fat that one slaughtered
for someone who owes a sin offering
for making the Temple or its holy food impure: what is the law?
Do we say: it carries karet, just like this one?
Or maybe: it is not fixed, like this one is?
phrases.notes: "Fixed" means the same animal for everyone. The טומאת מקדש offering changes depending on whether the person is rich or poor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב אחא's answer by restating רבא's Step 19 question as a change-of-owner question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does someone who owes a חטאת for טומאת מקדש count as a similar "other owner" for a חטאת of חלב?

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו. רבא's question is not resolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the topic and leaves רבא's question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No proof is found for either side. We do not know if כרת alone is enough to make the other person count, or if the offering also has to be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question stays unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: In רב אחא בריה דרבא's version, any change of חטאת type makes the offering פסולה. רבא's teachings are about a change of owner, and the case of טומאת מקדש is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question from Step 23 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a person who owes a חטאת for טומאת מקדש counts as a similar owner is left unresolved.

steps.title: Slaughtered properly, but planning to sprinkle the blood for the wrong offering
steps.stepSummary: A new מחלוקת: a חטאת slaughtered לשמה with the plan to sprinkle its blood שלא לשמה. רבי יוחנן says פסולה; ריש לקיש says כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if someone slaughtered it for its own sake, and planned to sprinkle its blood not for its own sake, רבי יוחנן says it is unfit, and ריש לקיש says it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new disagreement between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about a wrong thought that points to a later step of the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaughtering itself was done with the right intention. The only problem is his plan about the next step, the זריקה. So the question is: can a thought during the שחיטה about the זריקה ruin the offering?

keyTerms.meaning: He slaughtered it for its own sake, as the right kind of offering
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
Unfit / fit

steps.confusionAlert: Nothing was actually done שלא לשמה yet. He slaughtered correctly. The whole question is about his plan for the later sprinkling.

phrases.english: It was stated: if he slaughtered it for its own sake,
phrases.notes: "It" is the offering, here a חטאת.

phrases.english: with intent to sprinkle its blood not for its own sake,
Rabbi Yochanan says: it is unfit,
and Reish Lakish says: it is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: שְׁחָטָהּ לִשְׁמָהּ, לִזְרוֹק דָּמָהּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the תיקו that closed רבא's question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: an offering slaughtered לשמה with intent to sprinkle שלא לשמה is פסולה. ריש לקיש: it is כשרה.

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן says it is unfit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that a thought during one עבודה about another עבודה counts, and he learns this from מחשבת פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says it is unfit because we can have a thought from one service about another service, and we learn this from the thought of פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With פיגול, a person who thinks during one עבודה about eating the offering at the wrong time ruins it, even though the eating comes later. רבי יוחנן says a wrong שלא לשמה thought works the same way: a plan during the שחיטה about the later זריקה can disqualify the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: A thought during one part of the service can be about another part and still count
We learn it, from a similar case
Planning, during the service, to eat the offering after its allowed time; this ruins the offering

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says it is unfit
because one can have intent from one rite to another rite,
phrases.notes: He means: while doing the שחיטה, a plan about the זריקה still counts.

phrases.english: and we derive this from the intent of פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר פְּסוּלָה – מְחַשְּׁבִין מֵעֲבוֹדָה לַעֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for רבי יוחנן's side of the מחלוקת in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thought from one עבודה about another counts, learned from מחשבת פיגול.

steps.title: Why ריש לקיש says it is fit
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש holds that a thought during one עבודה about another עבודה does not count, and he does not learn from פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says it is fit because we cannot have a thought from one service about another service, and we do not learn this from the thought of פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind ריש לקיש's ruling, the exact opposite of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש holds that a thought during one עבודה about a different, later עבודה does not count. He also refuses to learn this case from מחשבת פיגול. So a wrong plan about the later זריקה, made during a proper שחיטה, does not ruin the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: One cannot think, meaning such a thought does not count
And we do not learn from that case

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish says it is fit
because one cannot have intent from one rite to another rite,
and we do not derive this from the intent of פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר כְּשֵׁירָה – אֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין מֵעֲבוֹדָה לַעֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives ריש לקיש's reasoning, mirroring step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thought from one עבודה about another does not count for שלא לשמה. It is not learned from פיגול.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole מחלוקת depends on one question: does a wrong thought during one step about a later step count? רבי יוחנן says yes, like פיגול. ריש לקיש says no.

steps.title: They follow their usual reasoning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש are each following their own known approach, and introduces another מחלוקת to show this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they follow their own reasoning, as it was stated:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to bring another place where רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue in the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is ruled here yet. The גמרא is telling us that this מחלוקת is not a one-time argument. It fits a pattern each of them holds, which the next quoted מחלוקת will show.

keyTerms.meaning: And they follow their own usual reasoning
Reason, line of thinking

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning,
as it was stated:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the מחלוקת just explained to another known מחלוקת of the same two אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two positions match each אמורא's consistent approach elsewhere.
